cards.text: We arrived {{c1::in}} Riyadh late last night.
cards.rule: arrive in + a city or country (an area); arrive at + a building or point. Never arrive to.

cards.text: What time does your flight arrive {{c1::in}} London?
cards.rule: arrive in + a city or country (an area); arrive at + a building or point. Never arrive to.

cards.text: What time did you arrive {{c1::at}} the hotel?
cards.rule: arrive in + a city or country (an area); arrive at + a building or point. Never arrive to.

cards.text: We arrived {{c1::at}} the station just as the train was leaving.
cards.rule: arrive in + a city or country (an area); arrive at + a building or point. Never arrive to.

cards.text: We didn't arrive {{c1::Ø}} home until midnight.
cards.rule: Ø = no preposition before home, here, there: arrive home, get home, go home.

cards.text: I'll meet you {{c1::at}} the airport.
cards.rule: at = a point or meeting place. in the airport only if you mean inside the building.

cards.text: Let's meet {{c1::at}} the entrance.
cards.rule: at = a point or meeting place. in the airport only if you mean inside the building.

cards.text: Our flat is {{c1::on}} the third floor.
cards.rule: on = a surface or level you stand on, so floors take on.

cards.text: The toilets are {{c1::on}} the ground floor.
cards.rule: on = a surface or level you stand on, so floors take on.

cards.text: She got {{c1::on}} the wrong bus.
cards.rule: on / off buses, trains, planes and ships (you can stand up and walk about). in / into / out of cars and taxis.

cards.text: We got {{c1::off}} the train at the wrong station.
cards.rule: on / off buses, trains, planes and ships (you can stand up and walk about). in / into / out of cars and taxis.

cards.text: She jumped {{c1::out of}} the taxi and ran.
cards.rule: on / off buses, trains, planes and ships (you can stand up and walk about). in / into / out of cars and taxis.

cards.text: Can you send it {{c1::by}} Thursday? That's the latest I can take it.
cards.rule: by = no later than (a deadline). until = continuing up to that time. on Thursday = on that day only.

cards.text: Please let me know {{c1::by}} the end of the week.
cards.rule: by = no later than (a deadline). until = continuing up to that time. on Thursday = on that day only.

cards.text: I need to be home {{c1::by}} six.
cards.rule: by = no later than (a deadline). until = continuing up to that time. on Thursday = on that day only.

cards.text: The shop is open {{c1::until}} nine tonight.
cards.rule: by = no later than (a deadline). until = continuing up to that time. on Thursday = on that day only.

cards.text: What did you do {{c1::at}} the weekend?
cards.rule: British at the weekend; American on the weekend; over the weekend works in both. Never in.

cards.text: I'm seeing them {{c1::at}} the weekend.
cards.rule: British at the weekend; American on the weekend; over the weekend works in both. Never in.

cards.text: {{c1::In}} the end, we decided to stay at home.
cards.rule: in the end = finally, after some time. at the end of + something = at its final point. At the end of the day = when everything is considered.

cards.text: I cried {{c1::at}} the end of the film.
cards.rule: in the end = finally, after some time. at the end of + something = at its final point. At the end of the day = when everything is considered.

cards.text: {{c1::At}} the end of the day, it's your decision.
cards.rule: in the end = finally, after some time. at the end of + something = at its final point. At the end of the day = when everything is considered.

cards.text: He accused me {{c1::of}} lying.
cards.rule: accuse someone of (doing) something. Compare blame someone for something.

cards.text: They accused him {{c1::of}} stealing the money.
cards.rule: accuse someone of (doing) something. Compare blame someone for something.

cards.text: She blamed me {{c1::for}} the mistake.
cards.rule: accuse someone of (doing) something. Compare blame someone for something.

cards.text: Her attitude {{c1::to}} her job has really changed.
cards.rule: attitude to or towards: both are fine in British English.

cards.text: Everyone noticed his attitude {{c1::towards}} the new manager.
cards.rule: attitude to or towards: both are fine in British English.

cards.text: She entered {{c1::Ø}} the room without knocking.
cards.rule: Ø = no preposition. enter, attend, reach, discuss, contact, phone, approach take a direct object. (enter into = begin, as in enter into an agreement.)

cards.text: Please don't enter {{c1::Ø}} the building after ten.
cards.rule: Ø = no preposition. enter, attend, reach, discuss, contact, phone, approach take a direct object. (enter into = begin, as in enter into an agreement.)

cards.text: Did you attend {{c1::Ø}} the meeting yesterday?
cards.rule: Ø = no preposition. enter, attend, reach, discuss, contact, phone, approach take a direct object. (enter into = begin, as in enter into an agreement.)

cards.text: Over two hundred people attended {{c1::Ø}} the conference.
cards.rule: Ø = no preposition. enter, attend, reach, discuss, contact, phone, approach take a direct object. (enter into = begin, as in enter into an agreement.)

cards.text: We reached {{c1::Ø}} the top just before sunset.
cards.rule: Ø = no preposition. enter, attend, reach, discuss, contact, phone, approach take a direct object. (enter into = begin, as in enter into an agreement.)

cards.text: What time will we reach {{c1::Ø}} the coast?
cards.rule: Ø = no preposition. enter, attend, reach, discuss, contact, phone, approach take a direct object. (enter into = begin, as in enter into an agreement.)

cards.text: I'll see you {{c1::on}} Monday morning, then.
cards.rule: on + a day, even with morning, evening or night (on Monday morning). in the morning on its own; at night.

cards.text: Shall we meet {{c1::on}} Friday evening?
cards.rule: on + a day, even with morning, evening or night (on Monday morning). in the morning on its own; at night.

cards.text: I work best {{c1::in}} the morning.
cards.rule: on + a day, even with morning, evening or night (on Monday morning). in the morning on its own; at night.

cards.text: There's no easy solution {{c1::to}} this problem.
cards.rule: solution / answer / key to something.

cards.text: What's the answer {{c1::to}} question five?
cards.rule: solution / answer / key to something.
